scope: sampled visual and story review; ASR and measured signal support; no validated audio listening
product_from_film: Astrocade is presented as a platform for playing, creating and sharing games.
explains_well: The founders turn their creation claim into a small story where one makes a game and the other becomes distracted playing it.
unclear: The game-making input and settings are too small to follow, so the film shows a creation claim and playable result without explaining the build step.
scenario: Browse games and make a game on a phone to share with another person.
product_clear_basis: A phone gallery shows many game cards; later creator and founder scenes add the creation role.

lessons.keep: Use a human handoff to make a generated result feel worth trying.
lessons.avoid: Avoid making easy creation depend on unreadable controls and a spoken claim.
lessons.open: Exact creation input, time-to-result, counters, funding/reward claims, effects production and all audio remain unverified.
try: Show one person creating a Tin campaign and another opening its finished preview during a conversation.
Keep the creation prompt visible beside the result before returning to character reactions.

comparison.story: Frame entertainment through familiar phone habits. → Present discovery as entering a new world; exact disappearance transition unverified. → Establish scale and variety. → Invite creators with varied interests. → Explain the platform and announce funding. → Turn the creation promise into a demonstration story. → Show the created game as engaging entertainment.
comparison.motion: Purple glow, floating panels, numeric counters and changing game states give the film movement. Precise portal and fragment transitions are not established by 1 fps samples. Sampling scope: 1 fps unless a closer window is recorded.
